newsitem.title: GHANA: SOCCER-GHANA FACE BATTLE TO REACH FRANCE 98 SAYS NEW COACH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GHANA FACE BATTLE TO REACH FRANCE 98 SAYS NEW COACH.

text.p: Ghana took a significant step in their bid to reach the World Cup finals for the first time when they named Dutchman Rinus Israel as their new national soccer team coach on Friday.

Israel, a member of the Feyenoord team which won the European Cup in 1970 and who subsequently coached Feyenoord, Dynamo Bucharest and the Dutch under-21 squad, replaces Sam Arday who stays on as one of his assistant coaches.
But Israel, who won 47 caps for the Netherlands, pulled no punches about Ghana's chances of qualifying for the finals in France next year, admitting he had a tough task ahead of him.
"Ghana has not started its qualifying campaign too well," said the 54-year-old Dutchman, whose first qualifier will be against Sierra Leone on April 6.
Ghana drew 1-1 in Gabon and were then held 0-0 at home by Morocco in their opening second round matches.
"Ghana does have some excellent players," he said. "But if you want to qualify for France you have to at least win your home matches."
Israel said he would spend much of his time assessing Ghanaian professionals working in Europe.
"I will also be in Ghana to find out how soccer is played here, what Ghana's soccer culture is and I will be working closely together with Sam Arday," he said.

Ghana, who have been African champions four times and whose junior sides regularly do well in international age-group tournaments, have never succeeded in reaching the World Cup finals. They first entered the competiton in 1962.
